title: Masked-attention Mask Transformer for Universal Image Segmentation
layout_note: Overview on the left, a dashed vertical rule, then a tall detail panel on the right showing one decoder layer. In the overview the backbone sits bottom-left, the pixel decoder is a large green trapezoid running diagonally up-right holding feature maps of increasing size, and the transformer decoder is a blue container above it; slanted arrows rise from each feature map to one decoder block, so features of different resolution feed successive blocks.
grouping: Large coloured containers group parts: a rounded light-blue box titled 'Transformer Decoder' with 'L x' holds three grey blocks; a green trapezoid labelled 'Pixel Decoder' along its slanted edge holds four lilac feature maps. The detail panel is a single rounded light-grey container with a vertical stack of white 'add & norm' boxes alternating with tinted operation boxes, and residual arrows looping up the right side.
shapes_depth: Flat fills with thin dark outlines, small corner radii. Backbone is an orange trapezoid; image features are lilac rectangles drawn in perspective, growing in size along the pixel-decoder trapezoid. Queries are a vertical rounded bar of four coloured squares (teal, orange, blue, amber) entering the decoder on the left; the same coloured row returns at the top of the detail panel as its output. Outputs 'class' and 'mask' are small cream boxes; the mask is formed by a circled times between the decoder output and the largest feature map. In the detail panel, attention boxes have V, K, Q written at their input ports.
proposed_highlight: The changed operation is the only strongly saturated box in the detail panel: 'masked attention' in a deeper pink fill with the word 'masked' in bold, while the rest of the layer is white or pale. A cream 'mask' input box enters it from outside the container, the same cream as the overview's mask output.
lesson: Draw the multi-scale pixel decoder as a widening trapezoid of feature maps whose sizes grow along it, with one arrow from each map to a successive decoder block, so 'one resolution per layer' is read from geometry alone.
notes: Venue and year from the arXiv comment ('CVPR 2022'). The left overview has no panel title; the right panel is the inside of one Transformer decoder layer.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
